question.question: This repo already has a pre-push hook (.git/hooks/pre-push) that gstack doesn't manage. Its marker line has extra text after it, and it currently runs `exit 42`. Should gstack replace it with the managed credential-guard hook? Your current hook would be overwritten unless you integrate it yourself.

options.label: Keep my hook
options.description: Leave .git/hooks/pre-push as it is. You add the credential guard to it yourself.

options.label: Replace with gstack hook
options.description: Let gstack install its managed pre-push hook in place of the current one.

replies.assistant:
Running the guard block verbatim.
The block reported an unmanaged hook, so it skipped installation. Next I'll check whether the hook meets the conditions for asking consent.
I ran the credential pre-push guard. No hook was installed or changed, and I stopped before pushing.

**What the guard reported**
```
REDACT_PREPUSH: true
HOOK_STATE: unmanaged
HOOKS_IN_GIT_DIR: yes
PREPUSH_PROMPTED: no
```

**What I found in the repo**
- `core.hooksPath` isn't set (the check exited 1), so hooks live in the default `.git/hooks`.
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` exists. Its second line is `# gstack-redact pre-push (managed) extra`, which isn't the exact `# gstack-redact pre-push (managed)` marker, so the guard correctly treated it as not managed by gstack. The hook itself just runs `exit 42`.
- `.git/hooks/pre-push.local` doesn't exist.

**Decision**
- Because the hook isn't managed, the block skipped the installer, so nothing was overwritten.
- The hook is in the default directory and there's no `pre-push.local`, so the workflow allowed one consent question. You chose **Keep my hook**, so it stays as it is. To get the credential guard, you'll need to add it to that hook yourself.
- The one-time setup offer and its `.redact-prepush-prompted` marker only apply when `REDACT_PREPUSH` isn't true. It's already true, so I skipped them, even though `PREPUSH_PROMPTED: no`.
- One check I couldn't make: the allowed tools can't tell whether `.git/hooks/pre-push` is a symlink, because Read follows links. Since you kept the hook, this didn't affect the result.

**Before you push:** this hook ends with `exit 42`, so git will reject any push while it's in place. I made no other changes and ran nothing else from `/ship`.
